method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited instruction address, operand, name literal, holder vftable cell, type descriptor name, RTTI name and call target was compared with those listings. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. The MEASURED facts come from the Lua 5.1 bytecode of the installed client scripts, parsed by a bytecode reader, and from scans of the executable named in each fact. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: The script binding map that connects Lua names to registered natives, including the receiverless names of the Global class, and static Lua call contracts of thirteen native registrations and four script surfaces: the character queries _getPos, _getDir, _getActorMainStat and _getDisplayName, the group queries _isExistInWorldMember, _getMemberDisplayName, _getDisplayName and _getKind, the item queries _getPackage and _getKind, the world query _getSpecialEventWork, the Math call _randomInteger, the player call _unlockPlayerControl, and the surfaces _isAlive, _math, _string and _table. Each row gives the registration site, receiver type check, declared argument and return lists, reads, client state effects, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish name presentation, group membership values, event work values, random seeds or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

tierVocabulary.STATIC: Read directly from instructions or data at the cited addresses.
tierVocabulary.MEASURED: Counted or parsed by the method named in the fact, from the executable or from the Lua 5.1 bytecode of the installed client scripts.
tierVocabulary.INFERRED: A name or role assigned from the surrounding instructions. The bytes do not state it.

framework.reference: manifests/fade_actor_group_native_call_contract.json framework, manifests/nameplate_group_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/scheduler_item_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the 0x00CC9D60 type registry, argument marshalling through 0x00D19A20, the holder receiver adapter, the invalid-parameter route, the return pushers, the world object chain and the yield request.

registration.note: The order of a native is its position among the rel32 calls of its switchboard, counted from 1. The last block of a switchboard returns directly after its registrar call or its skip path, so the call run of the WorldMaster switchboard ends at 0x00754E66. Each registrar listed here has one rel32 caller in .text.

framework.holdersNote: The other wrappers of these rows are recorded in the earlier contracts: 0x00726460 (CharaBase), 0x007265C0 (GroupBase), 0x00726670 (ItemBase), 0x00726CA0 (WorldMaster) and 0x007267D0 (PlayerBase), all const. The invoke routines cast the receiver with 0x009DA6CC from LuaControl (0x01270B4C) to the target type descriptor. A null cast returns false without calling the callback.

readers.0x0071CCB0: LuaControl*, cell tag 4, a size test around 0x0071BB80.

cellTags.note: The tag is the byte at cell +0x0C. The constructors store 0, 1, 2, 3 and 6 there. The list builders select registry entries by position: entry 0 int, entry 1 float, entry 2 bool and entry 3 Utf8String. Which builders (0x0072BD30 for Utf8String and int, 0x0072BDC0 for int and bool) declare a two alternative Which was read from the loop bodies.

worldObject.chain: R is the address that 0x00CC7510 returns for ExecuteParameters +0x04. X = [R], Y = [X +0x04], W = [Y] and V = [W], the chain of the scheduler contract.

fields.Y +0x08: Object whose first dword is V. The player control natives read the dword at Y +0x08 and pass it to 0x0075B240 and 0x0075B250.
fields.Y +0x10C: Special event work store read by _getSpecialEventWork.
fields.V +0x17758: RaptureUserControl object embedded in V, vftable 0x00F90F64, constructed by 0x004DECF0 at 0x004DC1E1. Its dword at +0x18 is the counter that the lock and unlock slots change.

worldObject.tier: STATIC for the offsets and calls, INFERRED for the roles.

nativeKeySuffix.writer: 0x007634B0 builds the string from the literal at 0x007635B1 and calls 0x00CC96A0 at 0x007635CE. 0x00CC96A0 loads the engine implementation and jumps to 0x00CD7630, which adds 0x1C and jumps to the string assignment 0x00447450. The suffix lives at engine implementation +0x1C.
nativeKeySuffix.consumer: 0x00CE1750 is the registration call behind 0x00CCCAD0. It loads the suffix address with 'lea ecx,[esi+0x1C]' at 0x00CE179C, concatenates the registered name and the suffix through 0x0044AB90 at 0x00CE17A6, pools the result through 0x00CEDE40 and stores the pooled name at record +0x44 through 0x00CD29D0. 0x00CD7670 forwards the record to 0x00D07820, which pushes the name of record +0x44 as the table key and installs a C closure of 0x00D08000 with the record as its light userdata upvalue.
nativeKeySuffix.effect: A native whose registrar installs the name literal _getPosition is stored in the class table under the key _getPosition_cpp.
nativeKeySuffix.tier: STATIC for the call sequence, INFERRED that the concatenation is the table key and that the string at +0x1C in the descriptor resolver is the same string.

descriptorResolution.routine: 0x00D07890, reached from 0x00D07BB0 when a script assigns a function to a key that ends in _inl.
steps: It calls the assigned descriptor with no argument and two requested results, read as the selector string and the key string (0x00D07997..0x00D079DC).

A selector equal to the literal self (0x0110F034) selects the table at Lua index 1. Any other selector is resolved as a class record name through 0x00CD8870 and its class table is pushed through 0x00CD7A50 (0x00D07A08..0x00D07A45).
The key is searched in the selected table and then in its registered parents through 0x00CD7B00 (0x00D07A73).

A function result is stored in the table at Lua index 1 under the descriptor name with the _inl suffix removed through 0x00D077B0 (0x00D07AB3..0x00D07B5A). The stored value is the function found under the key, not a wrapper.
descriptorResolution.note: xivl-decomp:docs/script/lua-call-function-bridge.md records the same routine. This record adds the key suffix above and the census below.

globalSelector.engineString: 0x00CC96B0 stores the string global at engine implementation +0x70, called from 0x0078FF82 per xivl-decomp:docs/script/lua-bootstrap-chunks.md. manifests/lge_bootstrap_attribution.json lgeRootMetamethod records 0x00D099B0 as the __newindex metamethod of the root table. That closure reads the string at 0x00D09ADF..0x00D09AE5 and, when it is nonempty, resolves the class record of that name through 0x00CD8870.
globalSelector.census: global_u declares 25 descriptors with the selector global: 15 return a _cpp key and 10 return a _lua key. The 15 _cpp keys are the registered names of the 15 Global switchboard natives in manifests/nameplate_group_native_call_contract.json framework.registration.globalOrder, so every Global native, _isExistActor included, has a descriptor. The 10 _lua keys alias the Lua helpers print, tonumber, tostring, type, assert, error, select, unpack, pcall and xpcall. The script also defines the plain functions _getTutorialJudge, which calls the key _getStaticActor_cpp on the global object with 320006, and _getLanguage.
globalSelector.callConvention: The trampoline 0x00D04DA0 behind every installed closure requires Lua stack index 1 to be a table (0x00CF3740 tests the type code 5) and otherwise reports through 0x00CCFB20 and 0x00CD4FA0 and returns no value. A receiverless call such as _getStaticActor(24301) has a number at index 1 in the script, but the closure that the global name holds is not the native. The root table __newindex 0x00D099B0 stores the forwarder 0x00D084A0 under the stripped descriptor name, and the forwarder calls global[name](global, args). Index 1 holds the global object, a table, and the Lua arguments start at index 2. manifests/global_native_call_contract.json receiverlessConvention records the forwarder, the trampoline and the native frame.
globalSelector.tier: STATIC for the descriptor census and the trampoline test, MEASURED for the script census.

registeredNames.method: Scan of the callers of 0x00CCCAD0 in .text, taking the last name literal that starts with an underscore from the registrar before each call.
registeredNames.descriptorTargets: The 376 _cpp descriptors of the _u scripts name 366 distinct registered names. Every _cpp key resolves to a registered name.
registeredNames.notTargetedNote: These 27 registered names have no _cpp descriptor key in the _u scripts. _turnDir is shadowed by the alias of _turnClientDir. The check is by name over all classes, so a name that another class does target, such as _getKind on ItemBase, is not listed.

descriptorCensus.scripts: 26 _u scripts, of which 7 hold no code.
descriptorCensus.descriptors: 439 _inl descriptors in 19 scripts: 376 return a _cpp key and 63 return a _lua key. 414 use the selector self and 25 use global.
descriptorCensus.plainFunctions: 18 plain functions without an _inl suffix, among them ActorBaseClass._isAlive, a no-op DirectorBaseClass._getPos, the Debug wrapper _getInstanceName and _loadCutScene.

bindingMap.aliasNote: Each alias descriptor returns a _cpp key that differs from its own name. The Lua name is the alias and the registered name is the native. _callSuperClassFunc is recorded in manifests/widget_native_call_contract.json. The callbacks of _setPosition, _setDirection, _turnClientDir, _getExtendedTemporaryAllGroup and _setPositionDirectionInn were not traced.

unboundCensus.note: The count is the number of entries of xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json with an empty bindings list. The work keys are _assignForChild, _globalSave, _globalTemp and _memberSave. The suffix identifiers are _callServerOnCommand_cpp, _callSuperClassFunc_inl, _callSuperClassFunction_cpp, _defineClass_cpp and _defineClass_inl.

rows.behavior: Takes no argument. Resolves the receiver identity to the chara object, builds its world position record and pushes the first three floats. The record adds the position of every parent along the chain at chara +0x98. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback reads the identity from ExecuteParameters +0x0C, takes the dword W through the world chain and calls 0x0075C230 with a 0x10 byte output record. It then pushes the floats at record +0x00, +0x04 and +0x08 through 0x007489D0 on the container at ExecuteParameters +0x1C, in that order.
0x0075C230 resolves the identity through 0x004D9970 and calls 0x004CFE30 on the chara with the output record and the flag 1. No instruction tests the resolved pointer.

0x004CFE30 with a nonzero flag and a nonzero dword at chara +0x98 calls itself on that object with the flag 1, adds the four floats at chara +0x9C, +0xA0, +0xA4 and +0xA8 to the four floats it returned and stores the sum. Otherwise it copies the four floats at chara +0x9C..+0xA8.
The return list builder 0x0073CE40 declares three entries that each use registry entry 1 (float).

The four floats at chara +0x9C..+0xA8 are a position and a fourth component, and the dword at +0x98 is a parent object whose position is added. The roles come from the native name and the recursive addition. Whether a rotation of the parent is applied was not seen, since the sum is componentwise.
The writers of the position floats and of the parent pointer, and the run-time result when the identity is not in the registry, since the null pointer is dereferenced.

returns.note: Heading in radians, folded into -pi to pi when a parent exists.

rows.behavior: Takes no argument. Builds the same world record as _getPosition through 0x0075C230 and pushes the float at record +0x0C. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback matches the first part of _getPosition and calls 0x0075C230 with the same record. It pushes only the float at record +0x0C through 0x007489D0.

With a nonzero dword at chara +0x98, 0x0075C230 adds the float at chara +0xAC to the result of 0x004DD8B0 on that parent, then subtracts 2 pi times the truncated quotient of the sum plus or minus pi by 2 pi, with plus pi for a sum at or above zero and minus pi below it. The doubles are pi at 0x00F62F48 and 2 pi at 0x00F62FE0. With a zero parent it stores the float at +0xAC unchanged.
The return list builder 0x0072B390 declares one float.
The float at chara +0xAC is a heading in radians. The unit comes from the pi constants and the native name.
The writers of the float at +0xAC, and whether the fold keeps the result in a half open range, since the boundary cases were not run.

rows.behavior: Takes no argument. Reads the display name record at receiver +0x60. A record whose first dword is not -1 pushes that dword and nil. A record whose first dword is -1 pushes the Utf8String at record +0x04 and the byte at record +0x58 as an int. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback loads the record pointer from the receiver +0x60 and compares the dword at record +0x00 with -1. No instruction tests the pointer.
A first dword other than -1 is pushed as an int through 0x00584F70 and followed by a nil through 0x00748920.
A first dword of -1 pushes the Utf8String at record +0x04 through 0x007487C0, then zero extends the byte at record +0x58 and pushes it through 0x00584F70.

The return list builder 0x00741DF0 declares two entries. Entry 0 is a Which of two alternatives built by 0x0072C4C0 and 0x0072BD30, registry entry 3 (Utf8String) and registry entry 0 (int). Entry 1 is registry entry 0 (int).
A first dword other than -1 is an index into a name sheet and -1 marks a literal name. The roles come from the shape of the two branches.
The meaning of the byte at record +0x58, the sheet that the index selects and the writers of the record.

arguments.note: A member control, an IndividualIndex pair or a one-based member position.

returns.note: INFERRED: the world presence byte of the member, or false.

rows.behavior: Dispatches on the tag of cell 0. A control or an IndividualIndex is converted to a member position by a search of the entries at group data +0x84. An int cell is the position n - 1. A negative or missing position pushes false. Otherwise it pushes the presence byte of the entry. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The argument list is the Which of the _isExistInClientMember row, built by 0x00742FA0.

The callback tests cell 0 for emptiness and loads its tag byte. Tag 0 reads an int and subtracts 1. Tag 4 reads the control cell through 0x0071CCB0, which wraps 0x0071BB80, converts it to an identity through 0x00CC73B0 and searches with 0x006C3560. Tag 8 reads the pair through 0x0071CD90. Every other tag takes the false path. The client variant of the group contracts reads every other tag as an int and pushes false for tag 8.
The tag 8 path searches with the second dword of the pair, wrapped by 0x00CC9320. When the result is negative and the first dword is nonzero it repeats the search with that dword.

0x006C3560 jumps to 0x006C3320, which walks the 16 byte entries from group data +0x84 to +0x88, builds the identity of each through 0x006D3FE0 and returns the index of the first entry whose first dword equals the first dword of the key. The end of the vector returns -1.

A position of 0 or more calls 0x006C0D60, which jumps to 0x006C0C40. That routine bounds-tests the position against the entry count and calls 0x009D22B4 for a position at or past the count. An entry whose tag byte at +0x0C is not 3 returns 1. A tag 3 entry returns the byte at +0x64 of the object reached by two loads from entry +0x08. The callback pushes the byte through 0x00748870.
A negative position pushes false.

Entries of tag 3 are members that have a presence byte, and the byte at +0x64 tells whether the member is in the world. The roles come from the native name and the sibling _isExistInClientMember. The entry layouts were not traced.
The run-time effect of a position at or past the count, the writers of the entry tag and the object behind tag 3.

returns.note: INFERRED: a name sheet index or a name string.
Nil with an index, otherwise the byte at record +0x58.

rows.behavior: Reads an int n and builds the display name record of member n - 1 through 0x006C0D80. A record whose first dword is not -1 pushes that dword and nil. A record whose first dword is -1 pushes its Utf8String and the byte at record +0x58. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback tests the cell vector, calls 0x009D22B4 when it is empty, reads cell 0 as an int through 0x005819A0 and passes n - 1, ExecuteParameters +0x04 and a local record to 0x006C0D80 on the group data pointer at receiver +0x68.

0x006C0D80 calls 0x006C09E0, which bounds-tests the position against the entries at group data +0x84 with 0x009D22B4 and then chooses by the tag byte at entry +0x0C. Tag 3 copies the record at +0x08 of the object reached by two loads from entry +0x08 through 0x006BF500. Tag 1 resolves the identity at +0x04 of the object at entry +0x08 through 0x00CC7A50, casts the control to CharaBase (type descriptor 0x012709A4) and copies the record that the pointer at chara +0x60 addresses. Any other tag builds the default record through 0x006BF420.

0x006BF500 copies the dword at record +0x00, the Utf8String at +0x04 and the bytes at +0x58 and +0x59. The default record has the dword -1, an empty string, the byte 0 at +0x58 and the byte 1 at +0x59.

The push step matches _getDisplayName on CharaBase. A first dword other than -1 pushes the int through 0x00584F70 and a nil through 0x00748920. A first dword of -1 pushes the string through 0x007487C0 and the byte at record +0x58 through 0x00584F70.
The return list builder is 0x00741DF0, the same two entry list as the CharaBase _getDisplayName row, and the argument list builder is 0x00728C20 (int).

The tag 1 entries are actor members that read the display name of the actor and the tag 3 entries are members with a stored record. The roles come from the casts and from the shared record shape with _getDisplayName on CharaBase.
The entry layouts, the run-time result of a position outside the list and the meaning of the bytes at +0x58 and +0x59.

arguments.note: Work number. 1 to 8 select a flag byte and any other value selects a 16 bit value.

returns.note: A bool for numbers 1 to 8, otherwise an int. INFERRED: a special event work store.

rows.behavior: Reads an int n and the special event work object at world object Y +0x10C. A number from 1 to 8 pushes the byte at work +0x84 + n - 1 as a bool. Any other number pushes the 16 bit value at work +0x8C + (n - 9) * 2 as an int. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback tests the cell vector, reads cell 0 as an int through 0x005819A0, calls 0x00CC7510 on ExecuteParameters +0x04 and loads the object Z at Y +0x10C.
n - 1 at or below 7 as an unsigned compare calls 0x0075D390 with n - 1, which returns the byte at Z +0x84 + n - 1. The callback pushes it as a bool through 0x00748870.

Any other n, which includes 0 and every n above 8, calls 0x0075D3A0 with n - 9, which returns the word at Z +0x8C + (n - 9) * 2. The callback zero extends it and pushes it as an int through 0x00584F70. There is no upper bound test and 0 or a negative n reads below +0x8C.
The return list builder 0x00742120 declares one entry built by 0x0072C5D0 from a Which of registry entry 0 (int) and registry entry 2 (bool) through 0x0072BDC0.
Two other callers of the accessors split at 8 in the same way. The caller at 0x0057918F selects the literal true or false from the byte.
Z is the special event work store of the world object. Eight flags and a run of 16 bit values are the layout the two accessors imply. The role comes from the native name.
The writers of the flag bytes and the words, the size of the word run and the class behind Y +0x10C.

returns.note: An integer from the lower bound to the upper bound.

rows.behavior: Reads two ints lo and hi, advances the 32 bit generator state at receiver +0x64 and pushes lo plus the floor of (r / 32768) * (hi - lo + 1), with r the 15 bit output of the generator. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback passes ExecuteParameters and the address of the dword at receiver +0x64 to 0x0078D040.

0x0078D040 reads cell 0 and cell 1 as ints, each after a cell vector size test that calls 0x009D22B4 on failure. It replaces the state s with s * 0x41C64E6D + 0x3039 in 32 bits and takes r = (s >> 16) & 0x7FFF with an arithmetic shift.

It converts r to a float and multiplies by the double -3.0517578125e-05 at 0x00FE0578, which is minus 1 / 32768. It stores the product as a 32 bit float, multiplies by the int hi - lo + 1, stores a 32 bit float again and truncates toward zero through 0x009D6600. The result is lo minus that truncated value, pushed through 0x00584F70.
For lo at most hi the arithmetic gives lo plus the floor of r * (hi - lo + 1) / 32768 up to the rounding of the two 32 bit float stores, which places the result from lo to hi.
The argument list builder 0x00583CE0 declares two ints and the return list builder 0x00728C20 one int.
The Math switchboard registers four natives, _randomInteger, _randomFloat, _randomIntegerWithSeed and _randomFloatWithSeed, at orders 1 to 4.
The initial value of the state dword at Math +0x64, its other writers and the run-time result for lo above hi.

rows.behavior: Tail-jumps through slot 0x114 of the receiver vftable. The PlayerBase routine is a bare return. The MyPlayer routine calls virtual slot 2 of the user control object embedded in the world object, which decrements its lock counter. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback is the three instruction thunk 'mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0x114]; jmp eax'. The _lockPlayerControl callback 0x006DE7E0 is the same thunk for slot 0x110.

Slot 0x114 of the PlayerBase vftable (cell 0x00FD5F18) holds 0x006DEA10, which is 'ret 4'. Slot 0x114 of the MyPlayer vftable (cell 0x00FD7970) holds 0x006E3360. The matching lock slot 0x110 holds 0x006DEA00 in PlayerBase (cell 0x00FD5F14) and 0x006E3340 in MyPlayer (cell 0x00FD796C).

0x006E3360 reads the world chain through 0x00CC7510, loads the dword at Y +0x08 and calls 0x0075B250. That glue loads V and calls 0x004D7580, which adds 0x17758 to V and returns the address. It then calls virtual slot 2 of that object with the object as receiver. 0x006E3340 does the same through 0x0075B240 and virtual slot 1.

The embedded object is constructed by 0x004DECF0 at V +0x17758 inside 0x004DBF40 and has the vftable 0x00F90F64, whose RTTI name is Application::Main::SqwtInterface::RaptureUserControl. scriptSurfaces.behavior: Called as a method on any script instance or on an IndividualRef userdata. A live script instance resolves the method to the ActorBaseClass function, which returns true. A released instance resolves the key to the global function __lge_isAlive, which returns false. An IndividualRef userdata answers through a C function that asks the engine whether the two dword reference still exists. No registrar of the 0x00CCCAD0 shape installs the name.

facts.claim: The Lua 5.1 bytecode of actorbaseclass_u holds a function with one parameter whose instructions are LOADBOOL true and RETURN of one value, assigned under the constant key _isAlive on ActorBaseClass. It is a plain function and not an _inl descriptor. The script has no _isAlive_inl and the index lists no binding for the name.

The literal _isAlive at 0x0110F068 has one code reference, the push at 0x00D08658 inside the instance __index closure 0x00D085B0. The closure compares the key with the literal through 0x00445D60. After a true answer from 0x00CE1BB0 a match pushes the string __lge_isAlive (literal 0x0110F074) and any other key pushes the string whose pointer sits at 0x0130D50C (__lge_returnNil). It then reads that global through 0x00CF3A50 with the pseudo index -10002.

The embedded bootstrap source at 0x0110E680 defines __lge_isAlive as a function that returns false and __lge_returnNil as a function that returns nil. The source text was read from the executable bytes.

0x00CE1BB0 returns true when the byte at record +0x7E is set. A false answer sets the byte at +0x7E and returns true. Every other case returns false.

The literal _isAlive at 0x0110F204 has one code reference, the load at 0x00D1110E inside the IndividualRef userdata __index closure 0x00D110B0. A nine byte compare against the key pushes the C closure 0x00D11010. That closure reads the userdata, calls 0x00CE19C0 with its two dwords and pushes the returned byte as a bool through 0x00CF3320. 0x00CE19C0 casts the engine object to LuaTentativeControl and calls virtual slot 4 through 0x00CCCB20.

The byte at record +0x7E marks a released or undefined reference, so the substitution makes _isAlive return false for a script instance whose engine control is gone. The role comes from the tentative state writer recorded in the Lua class system page and from the xivl-decomp widget work page.

ledgerCandidates.note: These are the Lua names of the unimplemented ledger rows that this record gives a registration or a script surface, an argument list, a return list and a callback contract. _getKind is bound to GroupBaseClass only and the ItemBase registration has no descriptor. _isAlive, _math, _string and _table are not functor natives, so a client implements them as script and bootstrap behavior. A client that implements the rows still needs the writers of the character, group, item and event work fields, the sheet behind the name indexes, and the consumer of the control scene packet, which this record does not supply.

nextTranche.basis: Distinct scripts that contain a call, taken from xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json, with the call-site count as the tie break. Natives with a contract in any manifest or a wire-level record in a contract page are excluded, and so are script callbacks that begin with _on, the work keys, the descriptor suffix identifiers and the Lua level _callFunction. A name with no class binding in the index that is an alias descriptor of the binding map takes the class of its descriptor. The nine remaining Global natives (_canCreateActorByName, _getActorByName, _getQuestActorForCutSceneReplay, _isExistStaticActor, _prepareAllCommandStaticActor, _getUTF8StringLength, _getUTF8StringByteLength, _normalizeDisplayName and _replaceMacroCodeString) rank below the twentieth row. manifests/global_native_call_contract.json covers them and carries the refreshed order.

boundaries: These are static client observations. No live Lua call or retail-client walk was performed.
Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. The run-time order of registration is the switchboard order of the framework.
Script call-site counts are static presence in the shipped scripts. They do not establish which natives a given script reaches at run time.
The Lua bytecode facts come from the installed client scripts. Their sources are not redistributed, and the tracked script metadata holds names and line numbers only.

The callbacks that dereference a resolved identity or a lookup result without a test, namely _getPos, _getDir, _getActorMainStat and the item queries, were not run with an absent identity, so their run-time effect is unknown.

The invalid-parameter route ends in a process terminate on the evidence of the target cursor contract. The calls that reach it with an out-of-range member position or an empty cell vector were not run.
The writers of the character, group, item and event work fields were not traced.
These are client marshalling and state contracts. They do not establish name presentation, group membership values, event work values, random seeds or server behavior.
